rows.grounds: the heart-essence described in the preceding verses
the inner core or life of mantras
the physical or vital heart as analogy

items.question: What gives all mantras their living power?
premises: This power is the heart-essence of all mantras.
Without this heart-essence, mantras are inert.
A body without a heart is like something living but not truly alive.
items.inference: Mantras have vitality only through this heart-essence, just as a body has life only through the heart.
uncertainties: The exact referent of 'this power' depends on the immediately preceding verses (191-192).
items.plain_english: This power is indeed the heart-essence of all mantras. Without it, they are inert, like living beings without a heart.

rows.grounds: established in the natural, non-artificial heart
the whole of that person's activity

items.question: What counts as true mantra-repetition for one established in the heart?
premises: One who has risen into this uncontrived heart may do anything at all.
Even breathing or touching something is included in that person's activity.
All such activity is considered mantra-repetition for that person.
items.inference: For one established in the uncontrived heart, every action becomes true mantra-repetition.
uncertainties: The nuance of 'mṛśate' could be 'touches', 'considers', or 'reflects'.
items.plain_english: For one who has risen into this uncontrived heart, whatever he does—whether he breathes or touches anything—all of it is considered true mantra-repetition.

rows.grounds: arising naturally through the creative process, both externally and internally
that very creation for such a person

items.question: What constitutes ultimate meditation for such a person?
premises: Whatever is fashioned by one's own will, from the nature of creation, outwardly or inwardly, is a spontaneous creation.
For the person established in the heart, that very creation is not separate from awareness.
Therefore that spontaneous creation itself counts as meditation in the ultimate sense.
items.inference: Ultimate meditation is not a contrived exercise but whatever arises spontaneously, inwardly or outwardly, by one's own will.
items.plain_english: Whatever is fashioned by one's own will, from the very nature of creation, whether outwardly or inwardly—that itself is his meditation in the ultimate sense.

rows.grounds: people motivated by a desired result
a form taken as the focus of contemplation

items.question: Why do seekers of results meditate on a particular form?
premises: The light of consciousness is formless yet contains all forms.
Those who seek a particular fruit require a limited focus.
Therefore some particular form is adopted as an object of meditation.
items.inference: Meditation on a particular form arises from the desire for a particular result, not from the nature of consciousness itself.
items.plain_english: Since the light of consciousness is formless yet contains all forms, those who seek a particular result fix upon some particular form as their object of meditation.

rows.grounds: though reality is undivided and complete
performing the act of fetching water
by excluding other possible uses or shapes
from a felt need or inclination

items.question: How can a limited form be sought within an undivided fullness?
premises: Reality is undivided and full, yet practical action requires selection.
One who wants to bring water sets aside other forms and seeks a pot.
The selection is driven by a specific desire, not by a division in reality.
items.inference: Choosing a particular form is a practical narrowing within fullness, motivated by desire.
uncertainties: 'rasāt' can mean 'from taste', 'from essence', or 'from desire'; here it likely indicates motivated inclination.
items.plain_english: Just as, even though reality is undivided and full, someone who wants to bring water sets aside other forms and seeks a pot out of desire, so a particular form is chosen for a purpose.

rows.grounds: through the expansion of the fixed order set by the supreme Lord

items.question: How does a particular meditative form yield a particular result?
premises: The supreme Lord's fixed order unfolds as the structure of manifestation.
Within that order, a particular form is selected.
That selected form produces a corresponding conception or attainment of fruit.
items.inference: Specific forms yield specific results because they operate within the Lord's ordered unfolding of manifestation.
items.plain_english: In the same way, through the unfolding of the supreme Lord's fixed order, some particular form gives rise to some particular conception of a result.

rows.grounds: the divine power appearing as the whole universe

items.question: What becomes the object of awareness for one who desires no result?
premises: A person of full heart does not desire any fruit.
Without desire for a limited result, there is no need to fix on a limited form.
By abandoning limitation, the goddess appears as the totality of all forms.
items.inference: For the desireless person of full heart, the whole universe as the goddess becomes the living reality, without restrictive focus.
items.plain_english: But one whose heart is full desires no result at all; for him, because limitation has been abandoned, the goddess appears as the form of the entire universe.

rows.grounds: in the tradition or family of Kaula practice
from the overpowering nectar of supreme Bhairava energy

items.question: What counts as mudra for a yogin absorbed in supreme Bhairava energy?
premises: In the Kaula path, the yogin may be whirling from the surging wine of supreme Bhairava.
Such absorption is not dependent on a prescribed bodily posture.
Whatever bodily stance arises in that state is itself mudra.
items.inference: For the Kaula yogin absorbed in Bhairava, any spontaneous bodily stance becomes mudra.
uncertainties: 'āsava' is rendered as 'wine' by the legacy hint; it can also suggest an intoxicating essence or nectar.
items.plain_english: In the Kaula path, for a yogin whirling from the surging wine of supreme Bhairava, whatever stance the body happens to take—that itself is mudra.

rows.grounds: not depending on an internal stock of fuel
burns intensely, its fierce flames extending through all the senses

items.question: How does the fire of awareness burn without fuel?
premises: This fire does not rely on an inner supply of fuel.
It blazes constantly on its own.
Its fierce flames spread through the entire stream of the senses.
items.inference: The fire of awareness is self-sustaining and continuously illuminates all sensory experience.
uncertainties: 'akṣaugha' may refer to the flood of senses or the flood of eyes; 'senses' fits the broader context.
items.plain_english: Without relying on any inner supply of fuel, the fire blazes constantly, its fierce flames spreading through the whole stream of the senses.

rows.grounds: as they enter that yogin's fire of awareness
become the occasion for true inner oblation

items.question: How do ordinary experiences become true inner oblation?
premises: All beings and experiences enter the yogin's fire of awareness.
Their entry raises up the true radiance of that awareness.
By entering and intensifying that fire, they function as the cause of true oblation.
items.inference: In such awareness, every experience becomes an offering that fuels the radiance of consciousness.
items.plain_english: As all experiences enter that fire of awareness, they raise up its true radiance and thereby become the cause of the rite of inner offering.

rows.grounds: a person made fit by the descent of divine energy
having placed before oneself or recognized as present
should remain established in the manner described, as one initiated

items.question: Who is fit to stand established in this true inner practice?
premises: A person may be purified by the descent of the supreme Lord's power.
Such a person can be brought forward and recognized in this state.
That initiated person should remain established in the manner already described.
items.inference: The one purified by divine descent and truly initiated is fit to abide in this spontaneous practice.
uncertainties: The syntax of 'purobhāvya svayaṃ tiṣṭhet' is slightly compressed; it may mean the teacher brings the disciple forward, or the disciple stands forth.
items.plain_english: Whoever has been purified by the descent of the supreme Lord's power, when brought forward, should himself stand established in the manner described; such a one is truly initiated.

items.question: Why explain the full sequence of rites if each can yield the supreme attainment?
premises: From mantra-repetition to offering, each individual rite can give rise to the supreme attainment.
This means no single rite is absolutely necessary as the only means.
Nevertheless, the sequence has been explained in this way for understanding and practice.
items.inference: Although each rite can independently lead to the supreme result, the tradition still sets out the full sequence as a clear exposition.
items.plain_english: Although, from mantra-repetition to offering, the supreme attainment can arise in each individual rite, the matter has nevertheless been explained in this way.
